facts.content: Patient reports lower abdominal pain for 2 days.

facts.content: Patient reports feeling hot and sweaty.

facts.content: Lower abdominal pain is worse and tender to self‑palpation.
Patient noticed pink urine.

facts.content: Patient has an Implanon contraceptive implant in situ for approximately one year.

No relevant family history is reported.
facts.source_text: FH: no relevant family history reported

facts.content: Patient lives with two roommates and works as an accountant.
Patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

Patient has a 2-day history of burning, constant, subumbilical lower abdominal pain that is tender, with a differential of urinary tract infection, gastrointestinal, or gynecologic or pregnancy-related cause.
facts.source_text: 1. Lower abdominal pain, 2 days — burning, subumbilical, constant, tender; differential: UTI vs GI vs gynae/pregnancy‑related cause

facts.content: Possible hematuria with urinary frequency is concerning for a urinary tract infection or urinary tract source.
facts.source_text: 2. Possible hematuria (pink urine) with urinary frequency — concerning for UTI/urinary tract source

facts.content: Pregnancy needs to be excluded given Implanon use and current sexual activity.

facts.content: Start empiric trimethoprim antibiotics beginning today as a short course, with the patient to collect the prescription at the pharmacy.

facts.content: Arrange a pregnancy test prior to or with treatment to exclude pregnancy.

facts.content: Arrange urine testing to evaluate for urinary tract infection.
facts.source_text: • Arrange urine testing (to evaluate for UTI) as discussed

facts.content: Provide paracetamol as needed for analgesia.
Advise adequate oral fluid intake.
Inform the patient that cranberry juice may help urine symptoms.

facts.content: Advise the patient to return or go to the emergency department if abdominal pain worsens, fever does not improve, vomiting occurs, or other concerning symptoms develop, and to have a review in a few days if there is no improvement.
facts.source_text: • Safety net: return/ED if worsening abdominal pain, fever not improving, vomiting, or other concerning symptoms; review in a few days if no improvement
